question: How many advance votes will have been cast in New Zealand's 2026 general election through 29 October 2026 (the fourth day of advance voting)?

calls.reasoning: Reference: 2023 had the same Monday-start 12-day schedule; the Commission's page shows 339,032 for the first four days (2017 equivalent: 226,824). The NZ Herald's live 2023 report (204,191 for the first three days) was about 13% below the page's revised 235,415, so the live figure this resolves on may come in lower. Downward pressure: enrolment closes before voting starts, removing on-the-spot enrol-and-vote. Upward: about 850 advance voting places and advance voting now being the norm. Market check: no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market found.
calls.dossier:
- Electoral Commission 2023 voting-statistics page (accessed 2026-10-20), daily in-person advance votes, 2023 (election 14 Oct, advance from Mon 2 Oct): 2 Oct 65,845; 3 Oct 80,899; 4 Oct 88,671; 5 Oct 103,617; 6 Oct 110,674; Sat 7 Oct 154,111; Sun 108,375; then 148,476; 147,260; 166,716; 205,341; 260,219. Total 1,640,204. The first four days add up to 339,032 (20.7% of the total).
- Same page, 2017 aligned by days before the election (Mon start, 12 days): first four days 39,570 + 48,238 + 66,084 + 72,932 = 226,824 (18.3% of the 1,240,740 total).
- 2020 (Saturday start, 14 days, COVID): first three days 92,434 + 66,821 + 105,489 = 264,744; total 1,976,996. Not directly comparable.
- NZ Herald, 5 Oct 2023: 204,191 votes 'since Monday' through Wed 4 Oct (first three days), versus 264,744 in 2020. The Commission's page today shows 235,415 for the same three days, so live figures were about 13% below the later revised totals. Resolution comes about 1 day after 29 Oct, so a live or partly revised figure is likely.
- 2026: election Sat 7 Nov; advance voting Mon 26 Oct to Fri 6 Nov (12 days, same pattern as 2023); 29 Oct is day 4. About 850 advance voting places and about 2,300 in total (elections.nz / RNZ by-the-numbers).
- New rule: enrolment closes midnight Sun 25 Oct, with no enrolling or updating details at voting places. On-the-spot enrol-and-vote advance votes are removed. Hipkins says tens of thousands may be shut out; Luxon says enrolment is higher than last time. About 3.68M enrolled at 1 Oct 2026 versus 3.69M at the 2023 election.
- Advance share of all votes: 47% (2017), 68% (2020), 61% (2023).
- Status quo: the daily pattern resembles 2023's.
- Resolves off the Commission's informal daily 2026 statistics page (in-person, excluding overseas), not the official count.
- Event window: 26 Oct to 29 Oct 2026 per the criteria; as of 2026-10-20, 0% elapsed (voting not yet started).
- Searched for but not found: 2026 Commission forecasts of advance turnout; the 2023 number of advance voting places for comparison; any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: First four days of advance voting in NZ general elections with a Monday-start 12-day advance period (2017, 2023)

calls.reasoning: Reference: 2023 also opened Monday with 12-day advance period. Commission's current 2023 page (revised Feb 2024 to include specials) shows first 4 days = 339,032; but the informal figures published live were ordinary-only: 204,191 for 3 days vs 235,415 revised (ratio ~1.15; day-9 843,044 vs 1,007,928). So live-published 2023 4-day ~292k. 2026 resolves on live informal figures; enrolment closing before advance voting reduces special votes but Commission still expects ~700k specials overall. Modest growth from advance-voting trend and earlier enrolment deadline; possibility that 2026 daily stats include specials pushes upside. No market found (Polymarket/Manifold per harness; no Kalshi/bookmaker market seen).
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the Electoral Commission's informal daily advance-vote statistics for 2026 (cumulative 26-29 Oct, excl. overseas), as published at the time, NOT later revised tables.
- Event window: 26 Oct 2026 -> 29 Oct 2026 (days 1-4 of advance voting, Mon-Thu); as of 2026-10-20, 0% elapsed (voting not yet open).
- 2023 (Commission voting-statistics page, revised Feb 2024 to include special votes, excl. overseas): day1 Mon 2 Oct 65,845; day2 80,899; day3 88,671; day4 103,617; 4-day total 339,032; days 5-9: 110,674/154,111/108,375/148,476/147,260. Total advance 1,640,204.
- 2023 live-published (ordinary-only) figures were lower: first 3 days 204,191 (NZ Herald, Oct 2023) vs 235,415 in the revised table (ratio ~1.15); through Tue 10 Oct 843,044 (interest.co.nz) vs 1,007,928 revised (ratio ~1.20). Original total 1,376,366 vs revised 1,640,204.
- Implied live-style 2023 4-day figure ~290-295k; revised (incl. specials) 339k.

- 2017 equivalent rows of the same table (aligned to days before the election): 39,570/48,238/66,084/72,932; total advance 1,240,740.

calls.reference_class: First four days (Mon-Thu) of NZ general election advance voting, Electoral Commission daily statistics, 2017-2023

calls.reasoning: The 2023 calendar is an exact match (Monday start, 12 days, Saturday election). Informal daily figures were 204,191 after 3 days (58,308 on day 1), suggesting about 295k after 4 days; the Commission's later revised table shows 339,032 for those four days. 2017's revised first four days were about 227k, and 2020 was about 366k with a weekend start. Advance voting is rising over the long term, against the new pre-voting enrolment cutoff (no enrol-and-vote at voting places) and an informal-reporting basis that ran about 15% below the revised table in 2023. Median about 300k. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or any bookmaker.
calls.dossier:

Later days rose steeply, to 260,219 on the final day; 2023 total 1,640,204.
- Same table: 2017 (opened on a Monday) days 1-4 were 39,570 / 48,238 / 66,084 / 72,932, cumulative about 226,824; total 1,240,740.
- Same table: 2020 (opened on a Saturday, COVID year) first four days 92,434 / 66,821 / 105,489 / 101,438, cumulative about 366,182; total 1,976,996.

- 2026: advance voting runs Mon 26 Oct to Fri 6 Nov (12 days); election Sat 7 Nov. 26-29 Oct is Monday to Thursday, the same weekday structure as the 2023 days 1-4.
- 2026 law change: enrolment closes 25 Oct, and no enrolment or updates at voting places. In 2023 about 450k enrolments/updates happened during the voting period, 110k of them on election day (ODT/Electoral Commission). Hipkins warns that tens of thousands could be disenfranchised; Luxon says enrolment is higher than last time.
- Enrolment: about 3.68M (90.8%) on 1 Oct 2026, against about 3.69M in 2023. Roughly 850 advance voting places; more than 2,300 election-day places.

calls.reference_class: NZ general elections 2017, 2020 and 2023: cumulative advance votes over the first four days of advance voting (Electoral Commission daily stats)

calls.reasoning: 2023 had the same calendar: Monday start, 12 days, Saturday election. The revised table shows 339,032 for days 1-4. The live informal figures ran about 13-15% below the revised ones, giving about 295k on the live basis this question resolves on. Modest growth from the rising advance-vote share and a possible inclusion of special votes push the estimate up; flat enrolment and the earlier enrolment cutoff work against that. Median about 305k. No market found.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the data. The factual question is whether resolution uses live informal figures, which ran about 0.87x the revised table in 2023 (204,191 vs 235,415 for 3 days). The question resolves 30 Oct, so a live basis is likely, which puts the anchor at about 295k. Whether 2026 live counts include specials can't be settled without web access, so the upside stays open. The size of the trend growth and of the enrolment-cutoff effect is a judgment call; I landed slightly above Run 3, using a live anchor plus modest growth. I kept the runs' dispersion of about 150k.

disagreements.claim: Resolution value will be on the live informal basis (about 13-15% below the revised table)
disagreements.verdict: Likely, given the 30 Oct resolution date. All dossiers agree on the 2023 live/revised ratio. Not fully settleable, so some upside weight remains.

disagreements.claim: 2026 daily stats might include special votes
disagreements.verdict: Unknown; no evidence in the dossiers. Kept as upside risk.

disagreements.claim: Net effect of trend growth vs the pre-voting enrolment cutoff
disagreements.verdict: Small net positive (+3-4%), since enrol-and-vote specials were mostly excluded from live counts anyway.
